nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What implications does the method of cost-recovery have according to the findings of the paper?
nodes.answer: The method of cost-recovery has significant implications for the distribution of household welfare and can affect welfare maximization conditions for each policy choice.
nodes.paragraph: We nd that while ef ciency grows in relative importance as the magnitude of the subsidycost increases, equity still outweighs the ef ciency loss in many circumstances given likelysocietal preferences for inequality. Should policy costs be negative, a at-rate levy is welfare-maximising under all conditions. Keywords Energy Subsidy Distributional incidence Equity Welfare loss JEL Classi cation D30 D60 H22 H23 Q4 Q52 Q54 1 Introduction How should public policy nance energy subsidies? Considering both equity and ef ciency effects, this paper evaluates common methods of energy subsidy cost-recovery: a at-ratehousehold levy and an electricity price surcharge. Humes and N. Farrell has important implications for the distribution of household welfare, and identify conditions of welfare maximisation for each of these two policy choices. Using a 2015/16 Irish case study, we nd that a at-rate household levy leads to a gross annual loss in consumer surplus of e105m.
